extracted.intended_audience: academic economists and empirical researchers studying education policy and development-econometrics
extracted.subtask_description: Appendix-level methodological and robustness standards for an econometric analysis of the SD INPRES schooling program in Indonesia, including DID, synthetic DID, selection-correction, bootstrap inference, data construction, and robustness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating equation for school–grade panel (equation form)
rubrics_metrics.description: ysjt = β(INPRESj × Post1972t) + (Xj × Post1972t)′Θ + δs + δj + δt + εsjt, where s is a school–grade level and other terms are defined as in equation (1). The dependent variable measures mean shares (e.g., share of weekly instruction time devoted to subject material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify treatment as district-level INPRES intensity interacted with a post-1972 indicator; residualize or include predetermined covariates interacted with the post indicator; include school-grade, district, and year fixed effects; interpret β as the average post-treatment effect given these controls; explicitly state the dependent variable construction and subject categorization (appendix D referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of unbalanced panel at school-grade × district × year level
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an unbalanced panel at the school–grade (primary, junior sec., sen. sec.) × district × year level, including only years in which the given district had any school–grades enter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing the panel, include only district–grade–year cells with relevant entry data; document sample counts (e.g., number of district–years) and any exclusions (e.g., primary schools omission for Pancasila because not covered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed effects and interacted baseline controls
rubrics_metrics.description: All specifications include district fixed effects, grade-level fixed effects, year-of-entry fixed effects; and baseline controls (e.g., 1971 children population, 1971 enrollment rate, exposure to water and sanitation program, baseline numbers of schools) interacted with post-treatment or cohort indicators as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interact baseline covariates with post or cohort indicators (or year FE) to flexibly control for differential trends; report which interactions are included in each table; keep policy-rule informed controls (province FE, deciles) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clustering and robust standard errors (varying cluster unit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Robust standard errors are clustered by district (in many specifications), by district of birth for individual-level outcomes, and by village when village-level inference is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose cluster level that matches the unit of treatment/policy variation (district or district of birth for SD INPRES intensity; village for village-level analyses). Report clustering choice for each table and cluster-robust SEs in inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance notation and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: * p<0.1, ** p<0.05, *** p<0.01. Report coefficient, standard error, sample sizes, number of clusters, Dep. Var. mean, and R2 where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow conventional star notation and always show exact standard errors (clustered) and sample summaries (N, number of districts/villages, mean outcome).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference-in-Differences (DID) baseline specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard DID estimates include district of birth × survey-year fixed effects and cohort fixed effects interacted with baseline controls (1971 children pop, enrollment rate, exposure to water and sanitation, numbers of madrasa and pesantren in 1957). Sample composed of original cohorts (e.g., aged 2–6 or 12–17 in 1974 as 'young' and 'old').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly define cohort windows and 'young' indicator; condition on same set of baseline controls and fixed effects as district-level specifications; cluster standard errors by district of birth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthetic Difference-in-Differences (SDID) implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: SDID estimates use residualized outcomes (obtained using the same set of covariates as DID) and construct synthetic control groups using partially exposed cohorts (e.g., cohorts aged 7–11 in 1974).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residualize outcomes on predetermined covariates before SDID; document which cohorts are used as donors and which are treated; when using SDID, compute standard errors using an appropriate cluster bootstrap (Arkhangelsky et al. (2021) cluster bootstrap referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection correction: Heckman (1976) two-step parametric procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Parametric Heckman two-step is used when conditioning on those that reached a given level; the second step includes the inverse Mills Ratio and excludes a set of covariates capturing exposure to a compulsory schooling pilot program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the exclusion restrictions used in first-stage selection equation; include IMR in second-stage and interpret coefficients as selection-corrected estimates; report p-values on selection terms and diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection correction: Semiparametric Newey (2009) procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Semiparametric Newey procedure includes a cubic polynomial in flexibly estimated first-step probabilities; cubic order chosen due to consistency results implying an upper bound of 3 for effective sample size of policy variation (275). In panel (d), quintiles of all continuous first-step regressors are created to better approximate the selection function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify polynomial order by effective policy variation; create binned/quintile transforms of continuous regressors to improve approximation; report both parametric and semiparametric results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bootstrap inference for two-step estimators (percentile-t cluster bootstrap)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels (c) and (d) deploy a percentile-t cluster bootstrap procedure proposed by Yamagata (2006) and shown to work well with two-step selection estimators. Standard errors in those panels are based on non-bootstrap inference, but significance levels on coefficients and p-values are based on asymmetric percentile-t confidence intervals derived from 250 cluster bootstrap repetitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using two-step estimators, report bootstrap-based asymmetric CIs and p-values in addition to conventional SEs; specify number of bootstrap repetitions and clustering unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-study and pre-trend robustness (Roth & Rambachan credible sets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report event-study analogues and credible 90% confidence sets per Roth and Rambachan (2022). These sets allow post-treatment maximum violations of parallel trends up to m times larger than maximum pre-treatment violation for different m; the credible set at m̄=0 corresponds to baseline 90% CIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot event-study coefficients ± 2×SE; compute credible sets for varying m to assess sensitivity to departures from parallel trends; explicitly report what m values were considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization and dependent variable definition (per 1,000 children baseline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome variables for school entry are normalized per 1,000 children in 1971 (e.g., number of entering private non-Islamic schools per 1,000 children). Other dependent variables include mean shares of weekly instruction time, indicators for Islamic schooling at different levels, Arabic literacy, language use, and religiosity indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state normalization denominator and baseline year; define each dependent variable precisely and document data source and coding rules (e.g., subject categorization in Appendix D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy-rule informed baseline controls (flexible targeting controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include controls that informed the INPRES allocation rule: province fixed effects, deciles of the 1971 children population, deciles of the 1971 enrollment rate, and exposure to the water and sanitation program. When correlating INPRES allocation, include these in regressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition on the policy-rule variables to reduce confounding in allocation; when reporting correlates of INPRES allocation, include these controls and report robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional predetermined controls interacted with year FE for robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment baseline specification with predetermined controls interacted with year FE: prevalence of waqf endowments in 1960, Muslim population share in the 1972 census, Islamic political party support in 1955, historical Arab minority populations, occurrence of Islamist armed insurgency in the 1950s, indicator for compulsory schooling pilot sites, and pre- and post-1978 transmigration measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testing sensitivity of supply responses, include these historical/political/agricultural controls interacted with year FE to account for latent potential growth in Islamic education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-sectional historical checks and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Use district-level cross-sectional regressions on historical Podes administrative data (e.g., 1980, 1983, 1990, 1993) to relate number/changes in schools to number of INPRES schools, controlling for 1971 children population, 1971 enrollment rate, and exposure to water and sanitation program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple historical rounds to examine dynamic patterns; report level and difference-on-difference cross-sectional regressions and their controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exogeneity of timing tests at village level
rubrics_metrics.description: Test cross-sectional correlations between timing of SD INPRES entry (year of first entry or early/late dummies) and pre-1973 village characteristics measured in 1972 (e.g., presence of Islamic schools, waqf land, potential crop yields, coastal location, elevation, land area). Regressions include district fixed effects and report F-statistic for joint significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report coefficients and standard errors for each predictor, joint F-test and p-value; interpret lack of joint significance as supporting exogeneity of entry timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness checks and sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform multiple robustness checks: remove time-varying controls, use a shorter panel (e.g., 1968–1983), vary clustering (village vs district), and apply robust imputation methods for staggered adoption (Borusyak et al. 2024) when computing average post-entry effects τ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present results across these alternative specifications to demonstrate stability; explicitly state which controls and sample windows differ and report corresponding sample sizes and clustering unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of selection and outcome samples (cohort and household restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define samples carefully: e.g., cohorts aged 2–6 (young) or 12–17 in 1974, partially exposed cohorts aged 7–11 in 1974 included in synthetic control construction, restricting to individuals whose final year of schooling took place in a given school type for conditional estimates, restricting to co-resident children aged ≥18 for parent–child transmission analyses, and splitting samples by religion/Islamic-educated status for certain outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document each sample restriction, rationale, and resulting N; when conditioning on graduating at a level, adjust for sample selection using Heckman or semiparametric corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple data sources and matching rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SIAP registry for curriculum shares, Susenas (2012–2018) for Arabic literacy and other individual outcomes, 2010 Population Census for language use at home, Pepinsky et al. (2018) survey for religiosity measures, and Podes administrative data for historical school counts; categorize subjects per Appendix D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the source for each dependent variable and how samples are aligned (e.g., which birth cohorts are observed in which datasets); document any mapping/categorization procedures used (appendix references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation conventions for figures and event plots
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures report semi-decade-specific estimates or event-study coefficients with 90% or 90% credible confidence intervals; event-study plots show coefficients ± 2× standard errors with clustering at village or district as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label axes with year relative to entry, show shaded CI bands corresponding to reported confidence level, and state clustering unit for plotted SEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling of informal taxation and waqf substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate individual-level models for informal taxation: P(informal_tax_ivdt) = θdt + x′iβ + f(Islamic school entry_v) + εivdt, where θdt are district×survey-year FE, x includes age, age^2, gender, and f is vector of indicators for entry periods (pre-1973, 1973–78, post-1978). District-level waqf substitution regression of waqf_c_d / waqf_d = α + δ INPRES_d + x′d β + εd (truncated in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include district×survey-year fixed effects, use demographic controls, define f(·) as period indicators, and interpret long-run associations carefully; for waqf regressions, control for predetermined district covariates.
